headline: Religious leaders from the Vatican to Baptist pulpits are speaking out on AI, which the Wall Street Journal says creates a new political risk for AI companies.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a well-sourced feature on a growing social force, but it rests on sermons, statements and interviews rather than polling and nothing new was decided.
importance_line: What changed is that churches are becoming a channel for public worry about AI, which affects congregations and voters first, then policymakers, then AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, but the evidence is a set of sermons, statements and interviews, not polling.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that faith leaders, including Pope Leo XIV, whose May encyclical (a formal papal letter) compared AI to the Tower of Babel, and the National Association of Evangelicals, which issued an AI policy statement this month, are weighing AI's benefits against threats to human dignity, jobs and community, creating a new political risk for companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. A South Carolina Baptist pastor, Joseph Hutchinson, told the paper that anxiety about AI now outranks wars and the economy among the worries he hears, while other faith leaders said they want to steer the technology rather than reject it.
notes: WSJ page returned 401 (paywall). Full WSJ text by Tim Higgins read on Mint (https://www.livemint.com/global/ai-has-a-god-problem-stretching-from-the-vatican-to-the-baptist-pulpit-11791713038632.html), which carries it under the WSJ byline; url kept on the WSJ original.
